factions/deaths-head.title: Death's Head
factions/deaths-head.content:
Death’s Head
A biker syndicate that held the Backstreets of District 12 before the Stray Dogs arrived. They controlled
the district through checkpoints, patrols and extortion, and their reach had grown after the fall of the
Wing. They were the local power, and they were overpowered by an invading force from elsewhere.
Organisation
Territory is divided into sectors, each held by a Road Captain. Below the Road Captains sit the
sergeant-at-arms and the enforcers who carry out their orders.
The rank and file wear leathers, white shirts and jeans, usually with a cut-off vest. They are armed with
tire irons, wrenches, claw hammers and similar blunt weapons, and work in groups that hold ground rather
than hunting anyone down.
Armored bikers are the elite of the group. They wear boots, leather trousers, shoulder pads and gloves,
with motorcycle helmets and road goggles, and they are used to break a line or cover a retreat.
Prospects are the lowest rank, foot soldiers who hold checkpoints and do the visible work of the
syndicate.
Territory
The Backstreets of District 12, divided into sectors. The apparatus of control is visible in the streets:

Checkpoints at the borders of their ground, manned by armed guards who take a toll
Armed patrols moving through held streets
A warehouse district used for storage and supply

The Pound sits inside this territory as well.
The Pound
A detention facility used to hold troublemakers and anyone the syndicate wanted off the street. Inmates
were kept there for holding and, in some cases, for eventual recruitment into the Stray Dogs.
It stayed open on the Stray Dogs’ orders, with the Death’s Head doing the work of running it.
Conflict with the Stray Dogs
The Stray Dogs invaded Death’s Head territory after the fall of the Wing and overpowered them. Afterwards
the Death’s Head answered to the invaders, and carried out their orders while resenting the arrangement.
The Pound was broken open by its inmates in this period, and a representative of the Kurokumo Clan
settled that disturbance. Bosco, a Stray Dogs Pack Leader, was killed in the same event.
In punishment for the escape, the Kurokumo Clan executed the Death’s Head officers responsible. Road
Captain Jodi and her sergeant-at-arms Brick were killed and hung from streetlights, decapitated. With the
leadership gone, members began leaving the area.
After the executions
The local Death’s Head fragmented once its officers were dead. The Pound stands abandoned, the territory is
in collapse, and its remaining members are scattering ahead of the Stray Dogs, who have since lost their
own hold on the area.
Notable members

























NameStandingNotesJodiRoad Captain, SouthwestHeld the Southwest sector, including the Pound and the industrial areas. Killed by the Kurokumo Clan and hung from a streetlight, decapitated.BrickSergeant-at-armsSubordinate to Jodi. Held a checkpoint and offered surrender or a beating before a fight. Killed with her.VelderRoad CaptainHeld a sector in another direction. The sector is not recorded.
Equipment
Leathers, white shirts, jeans and cut-off vests, with blunt weapons such as tire irons, wrenches and claw
hammers. Armored bikers carry the same aesthetic in road gear and motorcycle helmets.
See Stray Dogs for the force that took the region from them.

factions/stray-dogs.title: Stray Dogs
factions/stray-dogs.content:
Stray Dogs
A group of tattooed enforcers that invaded and took charge of the Outer Backstreets of District 12.
Members have named their origin as the Backstreets of District 22, and an account of a night encounter
quotes one of them describing the group as the terror of that district. They hold ground where the fog is
thinnest, and the local syndicates that were already there answered to them.
Organisation
Testimony describes the group entering District 12 as six packs of roughly fifty members each. A Pack
Leader commands a pack. Above the leaders is a Handler, referred to by title only, whose name has not
been recorded.
Five of the leaders are named in testimony: Rocco, Marco, Vito, Valentina and Bosco. Valentina is
described as the strongest of them and as a known figure in District 22 before the move. A sixth leader
appears only through an uncertain recollection, offered as “Mario or Marius” by a speaker who admitted
he could not remember. No account places the remaining leaders anywhere in the district.
Relationship with the Death’s Head
The Stray Dogs arrived as an invading force and took charge of the region. The Death’s Head, the local
biker syndicate that had held the district’s territory and checkpoints, were overpowered and answered to
them afterwards. The arrangement is described as submission rather than alliance.
Because the Death’s Head were the locals, they carried out the work while the Stray Dogs gave the orders.
That is recorded as a standing grievance on the Death’s Head side, and it did not survive Bosco’s death.
The Pound
The Pound was a detention facility used to hold troublemakers and anyone the syndicate wanted off the
street. Inmates were kept there for holding and, in some cases, for eventual recruitment into the Stray
Dogs.
It stayed open on the Stray Dogs’ orders, with the Death’s Head doing the work of running it. Holding and
recruiting shared one building, and the facility drew recruits into the group that had taken the region.
The breakout and Bosco’s death
The Pound was broken open by its inmates. A representative of the Kurokumo Clan settled the situation.
Bosco died in that disturbance, in territory controlled by the Death’s Head. Accounts describe him
engaging four people, killing one and wounding two, before being shot down, with a swordsman ending the
fight afterwards. He is also described as having neglected his duties beforehand, throwing people
through windows rather than watching what he was answerable for.
In punishment for permitting the escape, several ranking Death’s Head members were executed by the
Kurokumo Clan. Road Captain Jodi, who held the Southwest sector, was among them.
With Bosco dead and the local leadership removed, organization across the region destabilized. The
Death’s Head fragmented within that area and the Stray Dogs lost their hold on it.
Bosco’s Pack Remnants
Bosco’s death left his pack without a leader. It broke into smaller groups instead of passing intact to
another Pack Leader, and its members have since been recorded scattered across the district.
One of these groups settled into an apartment complex. Lupo rose to lead it, and its members no longer
use the Stray Dogs name, stating that Lupo holds the leash. The group appears to be absorbing refugees
and smaller syndicates.
Notable members

































































NameStandingNotesThe HandlerHandlerReferred to by title only. No name recorded. Above the Pack Leaders.ValentinaPack LeaderDescribed as the strongest, and as known in District 22 before the move.MarcoPack LeaderNamed in testimony.VitoPack LeaderNamed in testimony.RoccoPack LeaderNamed in testimony.Mario or MariusPack LeaderSixth leader, recorded only as an uncertain recollection.BoscoPack Leader, deceasedKilled in the Pound breakout, in Death’s Head territory. His pack dispersed after him.LupoLeader of Bosco’s remnantsNow holds a group that has abandoned the Stray Dogs name.RossiLupo’s lieutenantWore dark glasses indoors. Attacked Pug over a personal grievance, blaming him and Burr for the group’s abandonment in the district. Lost two fingers to a ballistic knife in the fight, then was stabbed with a glass knife that broke off inside him. Lupo called it Rossi’s own grievance and said many of his people shared the feeling.Big SalMember, Lupo’s groupMet visitors on Lupo’s behalf and sat with him when Bosco was discussed.The tunerAffiliateInk specialist attached to a pack. Not a member of the group.
Augmentation
Their main weapon is subdermal ink. Each pack has a tuner who applies and maintains it. The tuner is not a
member of the pack and is lent to the Pack Leader for the duration of the operation.
A tattoo parlor has been recorded on the seventh floor of a building above Summit Accounting and Blue Rock
Holdings, and below a hair salon. The artist there is not a member, works with Stray Dog ink, calls the
group bad for business, and was not accepting new work at the last visit.
Prices quoted at the parlor:

Full body, double pattern: 3,000,000 Ahn
Per limb pair, two pattern: 750,000 Ahn
Single limb, single pattern: 250,000 Ahn, 200,000 for regulars

Credit is offered to anyone holding insurance, syndicate backing or a Fixer licence.
Observations
The ink does nothing until it is activated. Members engaged before that point are recorded as markedly
easier to put down. Leaders appear to be chosen for fighting ability rather than for command, and their
decisions in the field have been recorded as inconsistent. Packs keep to their own boundaries, and no
account describes one crossing into another’s ground.
See Tattoo Ink for the ink itself.

factions/unknown-affiliation.title: Unknown Affiliation
factions/unknown-affiliation.content:
Unknown Affiliation
An armed group encountered in the Backstreets whose name has not been recorded. Its members wear
shrouds and cloaks, and carry knives. They are not part of the Stray Dogs, which they distinguished
themselves from before any exchange took place.
What was observed
Two members were met in the same encounter. One was shorter and carried a knife and a firearm, and
fought before it was established that both sides were strangers to each other. The taller of the two held
a knife and carried jars of a yellow substance at the belt.
Both treated an approach as a raid, and defended a community they described as their own. The shorter one
gave this account of the preceding week: a force she called feral had come into that community, raiding
and pillaging everything in sight, with no regard for trade or talks. She stated that the same force had
been rampaging through whatever stood in front of it, and described them as dogged and vicious. She did
not know what they were called.
Reports of disappearances in the area predate that account. No name has been attached to this group by
anyone who has spoken of it.
The two were hostile on first contact and willing to talk once it became clear who the other side was
not.

locations/backstreets-clinic.title: Backstreets Clinic
locations/backstreets-clinic.content:
Backstreets Clinic
A medical facility located in the backstreets, run by a German-accented doctor with round spectacles, a medical mask, and mismatched latex gloves. The building is long and flat with a red cross above the entrance. Inside, a reception desk sits beneath flickering fluorescent lights — a cage of white doves occupies the chair where a receptionist would normally sit. The doctor speaks to the doves in a foreign language to calm them.
Services
The clinic provides advanced medical treatment including heliapoeisis therapy and fibrous mechanite treatments. The doctor is willing to work within a patient’s budget, though costs scale with severity. Expedited treatment options exist but come at a premium.
A gestator — a mechanical healing implant — can be installed for severe cases. The procedure involves surgical implantation and requires a recovery period. Upon discharge, patients are given a pill to expel the mechanites before they overbreed.
Notable Events
Burr was treated here after sustaining full-body electrical burns from electrified spike strips during the Death’s Head siege of the mechanic’s workshop (Day 7). Pug negotiated a treatment cost of 250,000 Ahn, which covered surgery, a week of recovery, heliapoeisis and mechanite therapy, and the installation of the gestator implant. Pug was given a key to the hospital room to visit during recovery.
The doctor found Burr’s response to the combined treatments remarkable, noting that no one had ever agreed to trial both heliapoeisis and fibrous mechanites simultaneously.
Connections

Koller — The doctor is familiar with Koller through the underground network.
German Doctor — The doctor who operates the clinic.
Key, Clinic - Hospital Room — Key given to Pug for visiting Burr during recovery.

locations/deaths-head-clinic.title: Death's Head Clinic
locations/deaths-head-clinic.content:
Death’s Head Clinic
A small pharmacy and medical supply shop located deeper within Death’s Head territory. The area is sparse — civilians are emaciated, pale, with sunken eyes and gaunt cheeks, and they avoid strangers on sight. Death’s Head patrols pass through occasionally, some members not even wearing their leather vests.
Description
The clinic is a modest storefront. Inside, the shelves still hold some medication, though they could not be called full. Fluorescent lights flicker but stay on. A tired man works behind the counter.
Inventory & Services
The clinic once stocked Helapoeisis G9 (HP pills) — powerful healing medication — but most of its supply was requisitioned by the Death’s Head for their war effort. A small foil sheet of four 50mg pills was still available for purchase at 80,000 Ahn at the time of the agents’ visit.
The clerk is connected to the underground information network and is familiar with Koller.
Notable Events
The agents visited the clinic seeking HP pills (Day 4) but could not afford the cost. When they mentioned Koller’s name, the clerk’s demeanour shifted — he offered to deliver the HP pills himself in exchange for Koller’s location and left through a back door. Death’s Head members arrived shortly after, surrounding the building. The agents fled, pursued by an armored biker through the alley maze.
Connections

Koller — The clerk is familiar with Koller and eager to learn his location.

lore/strike-face.title: Strike-Face
lore/strike-face.content:
Strike-Face
Origin
Before the Corps perfected kinetic-energy manipulation, the technology began as a simple ceramic trauma plate manufactured by an early, defunct iteration of what was then K Corp — not to be confused with the present-day K Corp, which produces the Heliapoeisis healing drug and has no connection to kinetic-energy technology. The plates were stamped with a directional arrow and two words on the strike side: “STRIKE ← FACE” — telling the wearer which side took the bullet. Soldiers in the field began calling them “Strike-Face plates,” then simply “Strike-Faces.” The name outlasted the plate.
As Former K Corp refined its understanding of kinetic energy — absorption, redirection, dissipation — the technology miniaturized. The ceramic plate was no longer the vessel; the principle could be embedded into rings, chains, fabric, even tattoos. But the linguistic split was already complete.
The Split
At some point in the late corporate era, R&D formally divided the product line:























BranchDomainClean NameDegraded (Backstreets)StrikeOffensive — amplifying, directing, or delivering kinetic forceStrike Gear → StrikewearStrykewer → StrykeFaceDefensive — absorbing, dispersing, or nullifying incoming kinetic forceFace Gear → FacewearFaysewer → Fayse
The original plates became obsolete as a corporate product but never disappeared. They were too reliable to abandon.
Operational Tiers
Modern Strike-Face accessories fall into three functional categories per branch, regardless of form factor.
Fayses — Electrical Management
Defensive accessories themed around electrical circuit management: current, threshold, and load.
Fuse
Sacrificial. Single-impact. Destroyed on activation.
A Fuse detects incoming kinetic energy above a calibrated threshold, absorbs the full force, and shatters irreversibly. The wearer takes nothing. The accessory is gone.

Analogue: ceramic trauma plate
Cost: cheap, disposable, easily scavenged
Common forms: rings, thin chains, single-use plates

Breaker
Trips and resets. Absorbs a hit, goes dormant, repairable.
A Breaker thresholds similarly to a Fuse, but rather than destroying itself, it trips — dumping the energy and entering a cooldown state. It must be manually reset, repaired, or allowed to recharge before the next activation. While dormant, it offers no protection.

Analogue: steel plate — takes several rounds, then needs reworking
Cost: mid-tier, requires a Tuner or workshop for maintenance
Common forms: heavier chains, reinforced bracers, plate carriers with reset switches

Buffer
Always active. Dampens impact. Near-indestructible.
A Buffer does not wait for a threshold. It is a persistent kinetic dampener — absorptive material that bleeds force out of every impact. It lets damage through; it merely ensures the damage is never fatal in a single strike. Buffers are the most durable tier, and the most expensive.

Analogue: UHMWPE polymer plate — catches round after round, never shatters, eventually needs replacement
Cost: expensive, specialist
Common forms: suit-integrated linings, vest inserts, high-end bracers

Strykes — Thermal Management
Offensive accessories themed around industrial thermal control: heat buildup, venting, and dissipation. These are not fire — they are heat exchangers.
Flash
Unregulated thermal dump. Single-strike burnout.
A Flash converts stored kinetic potential into raw force with no thermal regulation — maximum amplification, all heat vented in one strike. Overheats the accessory, burns the user, and often destroys itself. The spectacle is the point.

Analogue: ceramic plate shattering on impact
Cost: cheap, dramatic, easy to scavenge but dangerous to use
Common forms: rings (Burr’s overheated bronze ring), single-use knuckles
Favored by: Stray Dogs — every punch is a statement

Flare
Thermal spike with cooldown cycle. Burst-fire.
A Flare delivers force in discrete thermal spikes, then cycles down to shed heat before the next activation. Hits hard, but the gap between bursts leaves the user vulnerable. More controlled than a Flash, still visibly aggressive.

Analogue: a temperature spike on a monitoring graph — sharp rise, sharp fall
Cost: mid-tier, requires venting period or external cooling between cycles
Common forms: heavier rings, gauntlet inserts, paired accessories for staggered cycling

Sink
Continuous heat dissipation. Always on. Never overheats.
A Sink converts kinetic force to thermal energy and disperses it steadily across its surface — no spikes, no venting, no burnout. It does not amplify as aggressively as a Flash or Flare, but it never hurts the user, never quits, and never needs cycling. A Fixer’s choice.

Analogue: heatsink — constant thermal load, constant dissipation
Cost: expensive, specialist, requires precision engineering
Common forms: suit-integrated panels, gauntlet plates, professional-grade rings
Favored by: Fixers — a working arm is worth more than a spectacular punch

Generational Layering






























TierWhat They WearWhoOriginalActual Strike-Face ceramic plates, legacy carriersWar veterans, old-timers, traditionalists. No fancy failure modes.StreetStrykes and Fayses in scavenged form factors — stolen rings, jury-rigged chainsScavengers, low-rank gang members. Whatever could be looted.ProfessionalPlate carriers with embedded Fayses; suit-integrated StrykesFixers, Syndicate enforcers, security contractors. The plate still catches the round when the tech fails.FactionSame tech, factional housingStray Dogs use chains and rings for visibility; Syndicate weaves it into tailored suits; zealots tattoo circuits directly into skin.
The plate carrier’s persistence at the professional tier is not nostalgia. It is pragmatism. When the kinetic layer fails — when the Fuse shatters or the Breaker trips — there is still dumb ceramic underneath. In The City, redundancy is not a luxury.
Vernacular
Modern Backstreets speech has long abandoned “Strike Gear” and “Face Gear”:

“He’s running double Fayses” — two defensive accessories stacked.
“That punch had a Stryke behind it” — offensive kinetic assist.
“Fayse popped” / “Fayse is down” — a Fuse or Breaker just triggered.
“Old man’s still wearing plates — swear to god, a Strykeface carrier from the war” — an antique, the technology in its original form factor.
“Needs a re-Fayse” — needs a replacement defensive accessory.
“He’s Flash-fried his arm” — overheated a Stryke and burned himself.
“Running hot” — a Flare mid-cycle, or a Sink approaching its thermal limit.

lore/tattoo-ink.title: Tattoo Ink
lore/tattoo-ink.content:
Tattoo Ink
Subdermal nanite ink, worked into the skin and triggered at will. It is the reason a Backstreets thug
with a pipe is a problem, and the reason the syndicates can field people who shrug off a knife.
The technology began life as a Wing Singularity, owned by a single Wing and worth what a Wing’s property
is worth. When that Wing fell, the patent died with it and the process went onto the open market. Every
workshop, every syndicate, and every back-alley artist has been copying and altering it since.
Essenai
The generic term is SNI, subdermal nanite ink. Decades of abbreviation wore it down into Essenai,
which most people now treat as a brand name. Arguments about whether Essenai is the best ink or merely
the most common miss the point. It was never a brand. It is the baseline, the way one word for a medicine
becomes the word everyone uses for it.
Essenai is what a syndicate issues to its rank and file, and what most of the Stray Dogs are carrying.
What decides quality
Three things, and none of them is a neat tier.

The brand is the raw ink. Where it came from and how well it was made.
The modification is the tuning. What an artist did to it afterwards.
The artist is the application. The same ink in two sets of hands ends up two different tattoos.

Good tuning can lift standard ink close to experimental work. Bad application will ruin the best ink
money buys.
Grades

Subpar — mass-produced, cheap, and whatever drawbacks it has were never engineered out. Some of it
is deliberately modified to imitate better ink: it runs harder and burns out faster. Sold to people who
do not know to ask.
Standard — does what it says. Its side effects are known and documented, though not always
mentioned to the buyer. This is what a person buys after doing some homework, and where Essenai sits.
Prototype — untested or experimental, built to order, expensive. It tries to remove a drawback
rather than live with it, and the cost of that has to land somewhere.

How the ink activates
Five philosophies, not five power levels.
Passive — always on, and the price is permanent. The user carries the tradeoff in their body for good:
slower, heavier, always armoured. It cannot be switched off.
Active, burst — primed and spent in one short activation. Fast to learn, fast to feel natural, fastest
to burn out. Needs intent and stamina and nothing else.
Active, toggle — switched on and held until released or until the user runs dry. No permanent price,
but a steady drain. Whoever relies on it has to end the fight before their fuel does.
Reactive — fires off a stimulus without being told to. An impact hardens it. A threat flares it. Fast,
and baitable. Anyone who works out the trigger can pull it early and leave the user open while it recovers.
Proactive — primed ahead of a condition and held until that condition happens. Needs a clear head and
a read on the fight. Devastating in a veteran’s hands, dead weight in a panicking one.
What it costs
From the parlor above Summit Accounting:

Full body, double pattern — 3,000,000 Ahn
Per limb pair, two pattern — 750,000 Ahn
Single limb, single pattern — 250,000 Ahn, or 200,000 for regulars

Credit is available to anyone with insurance, syndicate backing, or a Fixer licence.
Related

Stray Dogs, the group most often recorded carrying it

reference/faust-warp-train-dialogue.title: Faust Dialogue - Murder on the WARP Express (Intervallo IV)
reference/faust-warp-train-dialogue.content:
Faust Dialogue — Murder on the WARP Express (Intervallo IV)
Year: 984-11 | Episodes 1-14


Dante, please respond. There’s—


Dante, I understand your considerable degree of disorientation, but—


Your alarmed response and possible incompliance have already been accounted for.


Faust has indeed known this all along, as no knowledge is out of Faust’s reach. As expected, a solution to your dilemma has already been prepared.


The rearmost tail cars of WARP trains are all freight cars. That is where Mephistopheles will be safely fastened and transported.


And the LCB will…


… have the benefit of boarding as first class passengers.


The company’s budget is not a subject that warrants your concern.


That is the promotional language, yes. They are flash-freeze hibernation capsules, to be precise.


They have been designed to easily withstand the ‘true’ amount of time it takes for the WARP train to travel from point A to point B. The trip will be over in the blink of an eye for the passengers.


… Yes.


Dante, let us proceed this way.


Please elaborate on your exact definition of ‘safe’.


A flash-freeze hibernation device will put you in a temporary state of death caused by rapid cellular cryopreservation process. However, the rapidity of the process prevents damage to your cells during the phase change. Therefore, in most normal cases, this will not cause any issues.


Faust is aware that this model has fully resolved cell membrane-breaching issues caused by cryogenic density change or by ice crystal growths of hydrogen molecules.


Yes, as far as Faust is aware. Even if an issue were to arise during the journey, because everyone will be reverted to their states at the beginning of the train trip upon arrival, there won’t be any lasting complications from the said problem.


Indeed. As Faust’s talents are not limited to a singular field.


As a general rule, Faust does not err. However, Faust is also not a divine being.


There are certain information in the world that Faust is yet to have access to. Therefore, while Faust may speak the facts, what is said may not always align with the truth.


In order to prevent cases of unnecessary anxiety and misgivings among the Sinners, the history of accidents that has occurred aboard WARP trains will not be shared.


Then, let us hurry and enter our capsules before it is too late.


Is it anxiety, Dante?


Allow me to assist you. Stand as though you are leaning back, and…


Do not worry too much.


… We will meet again in but a moment, Dante.


Dante, you must wake up. Dante—


… An inconceivable situation has occurred.


No, we are not yet at our destination.


Yes.


… I believe we are currently stranded in an unidentified dimension. Coordinates: unknown.


………….


You are half correct, yet half incorrect.


Dante. I understand your confusion, however… perhaps an elaboration of our present circumstance is necessary.


Thank you. Then…


The Distortions themselves likely did not pose a problem for W Corp. Based on the available information, it can be determined that they would have all been neutralized as soon as the train arrived, and any transformed passengers would have been reverted to their human forms.


But…


That is the question for which we must discover the precise cause and effect of.


… That appears to be the most prominent cause of this misunderstanding.


However, we were given this master keycard that can open and close the hibernation capsules at will.


We may return to our respective capsules as soon as the contract is fulfilled and safely complete the rest of the journey as we had planned from the beginning.


That is…


… Next time, I will take your inputs into account.


… That, is something I must first discuss with Dante.


We must converse in a lower volume, Dante.


… My connection to Gesellschaft… I mean, Faust, has been severed.


I… cannot access Faust’s knowledge at the moment.


I mean it in the most literal sense. My access to Faust’s input and information, which has always been readily available… is completely severed.


One cannot completely dismiss that possibility, but even that is… uncertain…


Yes. At this moment, I am… limited to operating only with my knowledge.


I cannot discern the cause of this disconnection… More than enough precautions have likely been taken in case of interdimensional travel, but perhaps Faust did not take into account an occasion in which we may have to access an unidentified dimension such as this. Or, even if it was taken into account, this particular dimension may not yet have been subject to cross-observation.


If that is not the case, then I-no, nevermind.


There was nothing that suggested that my connection to Faust would be lost, not even as we boarded the train. To be honest, this is…


… a rather disagreeable situation for me.


… Understood.


And… to the Sinners…


… the fact that we are currently confined to a WARP train in operation must be a source of enough stress. I believe that sharing Faust’s current state with them would add an unnecessary source of tension.


In the grand scheme of things, yes.


By A Corp.’s standard time scale, approximately three days have passed since our departure.


As per the contract between Limbus Company and W Corp., I acquired the master keycard placed inside my capsule and adjusted the hatch settings to open automatically in three days.


As you were all informed prior to boarding, there is no way for the economy class passengers to enter the first class car; that is why this place has remained untouched.


However, cross-referencing my own deductions and W Corp.’s rather fragmentary explanations, I can assume that ‘the situation’ is currently under progress in the economy class cars.


Precisely. In my opinion, it is—


Please step aside for a moment, Don Quixote. It would be best if I observed it with my own eyes.


I intend to follow your usual flavor of suggestion, Heathcliff.


That there are times in which a physical altercation is preferable to detached ruminations.


After all… how could I deduce anything without seeing it myself?


… Don Quixote.


They are not dead.


Observe closer. The parts are all tethered to one another by something, are they not?


It appears that the flow of time has ceased in this space. Therefore, it follows that the… connections, that tether bodies to life and away from death, remain intact.


Yes. That is a most rational suggestion, Yi Sang.


If their severed parts are all connected… then it can be said that no matter how entangled their bodies become, it is not impossible to eventually gather their parts together to form a single passenger.


Thus, naturally, we can determine how and why the profession ‘W Corp. Cleanup Agent’ has come to be.


Dante.


… Indeed. I intend to collect further intelligence.


Are they Distortions, or… Abnormalities?


Is it difficult to be certain at the moment?


Faust may know… but I, at this moment, have no way of knowing.


There is no need, Dante.


Though the information you have provided me is rather ambiguous, it has helped me deduce something of worth.


And…


Collecting intelligence myself and creating deductions based on sparse information is quite…


… She appeared without warning.


Have you not left this car for the duration of the ride, Sasha?


Hasn’t something else of note also occurred?


… You have decided to protect them, despite the potential risk that they may transform as well.


… I see.


W Corp. has hired us to solve this case. We are…


Um…


Indeed… Fixers.


As you must be well aware yourself, contracts and contract fulfillment are of paramount importance for Fixers.


With that in mind, please recall that W Corp. is one of the most secretive Wings of the City.


This is the master keycard given to us by W Corp. I believe that it can open most doors aboard this train.


It is fortunate that someone like yourself is aboard the train. Your presence ensured that child’s survival.


Be like… what?


Eyes…


I have one last thing to inquire.


… That is quite an unsound decision to make for someone who claims to be ‘in the same line of work’ as us.


Have you considered the possibility that, once our contract is successfully completed, we could include references to a particularly cooperative Associate Office in our report to W Corp?


Were the eyes of the monsters you faced red, by any chance?


No, well.


It was a question of no significance.


Those entities are…


… What do you think those entities are?


Yes, and? Was there anything else?


Thank you, all. Your input has all been very helpful.


We are in luck, Dante.


I have read upon this subject as a tangent while perusing information regarding our next destination, moments before we boarded the train. And while that will be a useful element in resolving this situation…


… the Sinners have also been a very good source of intelligence when it came to categorizing and identifying important evidence from the available sea of information. Your advice was correct, Dante.


Nothing can be said with absolute certainty at the moment. However, this will be a good place for us to start.


… I will now present before you a solution to this predicament.


That will not change, no. However, what I am about to share will give you a better understanding of the purpose behind W Corp.’s contract, and provide us with the possible means of finding the method by which we may complete it.


It is very likely that the entity behind the incidents on this train, and by extension, every incident of the same nature that has occurred in previous WARP train trips…


… is a Bloodfiend.


… Yes. I see that some Sinners may have encountered Bloodfiends in the past. A long-winded explanation seems unnecessary.


As many of you have stated thus far, the entities we faced in this train do not appear to be ‘Bloodfiends’.


In a sense, they are dreg-like beings that have failed to become Kindreds… they are referred to as ‘Bloodbags’ among relevant parties, according to information I am aware of.


As it has been said prior, it is impossible for passengers to disappear aboard WARP trains under normal circumstances.


Though our reserve of intelligence regarding the WARP trains or W Corp. is vast, if incomplete, we could not find a possible exception to the above rule.


Within that reserve of intelligence, however, I have discovered that inserting a previously unseen variable into the equation allows for a formulation of a new hypothesis.


A more accurate descriptor would be to say that they are either dissolved or vaporized.


No matter the degree of violence the passengers may indulge in, no matter how severe the damages may be, the WARP trains can revert them to their initial states at the beginning of the journey.


Among several interpretations of the word ‘violence’ involves cannibalization, of course.


However, as the passengers’ collective time itself is in moratorium for the duration of the train’s operation, digestion is not a biological process that should be active. In other words, even the devoured passengers could be reconstructed.


However, such is not true for ‘Bloodbags’. Bloodbags are, by their nature, obsessed with blood; their existence hinges on supplying themselves with the blood of their victims.


And it is said that they must consume a minuscule amount of blood to maintain their forms.


If I were to continue my deductions… perhaps ‘consumption of blood’, for Bloodfiends and Bloodbags is a fundamentally different process from our ‘consumption of nutrients’ for energy.


To them, blood is a culmination, an entailment of something that forms the self, including but not limited to: emotions, ambitions, wealth, purposes of existence… Then, it must naturally follow that they can spend their blood at will, which is a process that is isolated from other biological processes such as digestion.


… That information is inaccessible at the moment.


This is only a speculation, however… I assume that a form of direct physical contact is needed to turn an individual into a Bloodbag. If such were not the case, then we, who are likely the greatest obstacles to this entity’s goal at the moment, would have been the first ones to be turned.


Indeed. If we are to believe the words of the Fixer from earlier, then there is a high likelihood that the horde is advancing in this direction from the back of the train…


In other words, continuing down the train cars will lead us straight to the Bloodfiend.


… Dante.


My apologies. The access to that information is prohibited at this moment as well.


… I may have been too reliant on Faust. In too many places.


He has departed the scene.


I see. There are multiple possible interpretations depending on one’s perspective, despite the fact that there is but a single scene. I will remember both of your inputs.


Yes, well. Good for them.


I am physically unharmed, yet… Hm. Yes, I am alright.


However, I do not enjoy this circumstance which we find ourselves in. It is as though I am casting nets to nowhere while lost and isolated in a blind sea.


… I could usually complete these deductions within moments after establishing a few basic cross-references between the accessible information.


… Is that so.


Although this is not common knowledge, there is a subcategory of Fixers called Bloodfiend Hunters who specialize in… yes, hunting Bloodfiends.


Assuming that information is true, it can be inferred that Bloodfiends are difficult foes that require a certain expertise to defeat.


He… must be the Bloodfiend who caused this outbreak. He is our target.


Do not let your guard down, Heathcliff. This entity has managed to turn countless passengers of this train into his Bloodbags.


This is rather curious.


It appears that this Bloodfiend leaves this car only on rare occasions…


… Yet we have seen signs of his insidious influence throughout every car we have visited so far.


Bloodfiends…


… What if there was more than a single Bloodfiend on board, one still capable of rational thought…


Don Quixote, watch out!


Kindred…


Are you even aware of the exact nature of a ‘Kindred’?


I see. A Bloodfiend’s Kindred is like a sub-entity of the Bloodfiend, similar in concept to sub-entities created by Distortions or Abnormalities.


It must have been desperation that drove you to accept that proposition without hesitation, despite the lack of relevant information.


… It appears that he has empowered himself by reaping their blood.


Don Quixote! Stop her, now!


Dante…


I believed myself to be trying my utmost to overcome this adversity…


… without access to Faust’s knowledge and intelligence.


However…


With our loss of the Master Keycard… the uncertainty of this circumstance has greatly exacerbated.


At the origin of this plight…


… must be my overreliance on Faust.


Indeed, among many, I am a Faust that believes in uncertainty.


Our loss of the master keycard is but one of innumerable uncertain variables in the equation.


The constant is, however…


… that the Bloodfiend is just as desperate as we are.


Thus the only option that remains at present is to… compromise.


Very well. Then… Cassetti, why don’t we move this conversation to a different location?


Only I will accompany Dante to this negotiation. I will make my intentions clear now: Dante and I will not attack you there.


Yes. The freight car is immediately adjacent to this one; that is where we will further discuss what we each have to offer to one another.


Correct.


Dante… this will be my first attempt…


… at a ‘gamble’.


The connection has been restored.


Boarding Mephistopheles has… reestablished my connection to Faust.


No. And as I have stated before, this was a pure, incalculable gamble based on my own uncertain hypothesis.


This success helps me somewhat comprehend Miss Rodya’s fascination with gambling.


Now that the connection has been reestablished, I would like to make a complaint against the Fausts in the Gesellschaft management regarding the fact that they neglected to list the information pertaining to the loss of connection within the interiors of the WARP trains, however…


… finding a solution to this situation takes precedence. I have much reason to believe that their omission was done on purpose, but… I hope such is not the case.


… Let us discuss the details of our compromise. What are you willing to accept in return for the master keycard?


Like nothing happened…


Our memories and any signs of battle will be entirely erased upon our arrival. We will have no way to relay our news, whether one of success or failure.


If we had the means to defeat him, then at least W Corp. would inform us that our contract was successful after the fact. However…


… this current scenario will leave us with nothing to show for, not even the smallest hint, and the contract will end in failure.


However, what takes precedence over the contract is you and the Sinners’ psychological stability.


Certainly, you are aware that your suggestion is no solution at all, Don Quixote.


… Oh, I did not expect this to be the solution…


… According to this information I had viewed in the past, and once again just now, it’s…


Mm. … Dante. Take cover behind me and remain absolutely still.


And please, do note that the other Sinners must never hear a word of what is about to happ—


She appears to be in a state of deep slumber. As she is not at a risk of death, she will be waking up soon.


The master keycard is not an absolutely necessary element to resolving this situation.


It will require approximately five hours to formulate and proceed with an explanation in a manner that will allow the Sinners to fully comprehend the exact ‘how’ of this methodology. Therefore, it will be delivered to you in a digestible, summarized format.


We can utilize the Backdoor of Mephistopheles.


To put it simply, we will spend the time at a space disconnected from the train.


The train should be arriving at its destination in approximately ten seconds, going by the A Corp. time scale. All we must do is to remain somewhere in our original dimension for that duration.


Yes. This is the correct door. Its safety is completely ensured.


I… did not bother verifying that particular information myself.


It is necessary for future endeavors that I gain the experience… of encountering something completely unexpected.


Now, please enter through this door.


5… 4… 3… 2… 1…


We are employees of Limbus Company. We boarded the WARP train at the behest of your employer.


Yes, we must have suffered from a momentary, collective hallucination caused by fatigue. Very well, then. We will see ourselves out.


Understood. Any and all relevant reports will be sent to W Corp. via LCCA, and…


Because it was the preferable course of action to having the same explosive demise occur to your body instead.


I do find it regrettable that you were made to turn the clock despite my knowledge of the high likelihood of my death upon that occurrence.


… That is something I have been aware of since the LCB was first established. The same could be said of Vergilius.


However, it was by the will of the LCA’s superiors that this knowledge remains withheld from the Manager until the appropriate moment.


… According to my private judgment, yes.


Well, as my connection to all communications, including one to Faust, had been severed. I was not in a position to receive the headquarters’ authorization for that action.
